directions.thesis: Everything new lands where the named legacy render already put it. Prerequisites become a gate under the promises, the discount ladder stays in the rail beneath the price, trial and cart join the rail under the primary enrol button, and the review block sits at the foot after the curriculum. The rail is a form, so it holds still: a buy box that animates while a reader compares a price is a buy box they stop trusting.
directions.primaryCta: Dang ky hoc, in the rail, unmoved from where the applied page puts it
readingOrder: rail: price, ladder, enrol, trial, cart
tradeoffs: Strongest: nothing that works today moves, so review compares additions rather than a rearrangement.
Weakest: the reviews sit furthest from the moment of decision, which is the one thing the new backend was built to serve.
Rejection risk: a reader who never scrolls past the curriculum never sees the rating at all.

exactProposals: NEW contract course-prerequisite-list + course-prerequisite-row, mirroring course-promise-list mechanics under a domain-correct name
EXTEND course-pricing-rail children with trial and cart slots, both optional

directions.thesis: A buyer who is not convinced does not read a curriculum, so the rating rises into the hero chip run and the review block moves above the curriculum. Prerequisites become a disclosure at the head of the curriculum, where they answer the question the curriculum raises. The rail collapses to a price-and-CTA strip once the hero scrolls past.
directions.primaryCta: Dang ky hoc, surviving into the collapsed rail strip
tradeoffs: Strongest: proof arrives before the price is compared, which is what the new review capability exists for.
Weakest: the hero rating must be ABSENT rather than zero when a course has no reviews, because zero stars reads as a bad course rather than a new one.

Rejection risk: the collapse behaviour is client behaviour no existing owner declares, and the collapsed rail must decide whether to keep or drop the discount ladder - keeping it defeats the collapse, dropping it hides the reason for the price.
legacyDivergence: The named legacy render puts reviews last; this direction puts them before the curriculum.
Legacy has no rating in the hero.

exactProposals: EXTEND course-stat-chip-run with an optional rating chip
NEW contract course-review-block, course-review-summary, course-review-row, course-prerequisite-disclosure
unmappedAnatomy: the rail's collapse-on-scroll behaviour: no locked owner declares a scroll observer, and the tier that would hold it today declares only static classes

directions.thesis: Split the page by job rather than by topic. The main column becomes pure narrative and the rail becomes the whole decision surface: price, ladder, rating line, prerequisites as a checklist, and all three ways in. A reader deciding never leaves the rail; a reader learning never steps over a CTA.
directions.primaryCta: Dang ky hoc, inside a rail that also carries the conditions of buying
readingOrder: rail: price, ladder, rating, prerequisites, enrol, trial, cart
tradeoffs: Strongest: everything a purchase decision needs is in one place, and the narrative is never interrupted by a CTA.
Weakest: it claims a prerequisite is a condition of buying rather than a piece of the syllabus. If that claim is wrong, this direction puts course content inside a buy box.

Rejection risk: the rail already declares max-h-rail and overflow-y-auto, so a long desk can push the enrol button below the rail's OWN fold on a short laptop - a failure the other two directions cannot produce.
legacyDivergence: Legacy keeps prerequisites in the narrative column.

EXTEND course-pricing-rail children with four optional slots
